journalName: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publisher: Royal Astronomical Society / Oxford University Press

entryTemplates.software: {authors}, {year}, Astrophysics Source Code Library, record ascl:{id}

notes: In-text citation examples on the current official page include first initials — '(J. Brown 1999)', 'J. Brown & P. Jones (1991)' — which differs from the traditional mnras.bst BibTeX output (no initials); verified verbatim on the Instructions to Authors page.
Three authors: give all three names at first mention, then first author et al. (roman, not italic); four or more: first author et al. always.
Multiple citations in one bracket are separated by semicolons; same-author years collate '(J. Brown 1992, 1995)'; same-year papers as 'A. Smith et al. (2000a,b)'.
Reference list: no bold/italic, no commas after surnames, no ampersand between the final two names; private communications and papers in preparation are cited in text only and omitted from the list.
Journal abbreviations: journal's own simplified list of ~20 frequent journals (A&A, ApJ, AJ, MNRAS, Nature, Science, ...); IAU standard abbreviations for journals not on the list.
No DOI-printing requirement stated; online links are generated from reference details, so details must be accurate.
Figure labelling should suit the likely final size of around 8 pt; all fonts and logos must be embedded in the figure file.
TIFF resolution at final size: 300 ppi for grey-scale/half-tone (photographs), 800 ppi for combined line/tone; bitmapped elements inside vector files need >=400 dpi effective resolution.
Panel labels (a), (b) must be embedded in the graphics file itself — not added via LaTeX (figures are processed separately from the LaTeX code).
Plots should have borders on all sides, fiducial marks on every border, and labelled axes including units; refer to figures as 'Fig. 1' and tables as 'Table 1'.
Letters must not exceed five pages; title, author list, affiliations, abstract, keywords, data availability statement, acknowledgements and references are excluded from that limit.
Papers have no page limits but should be concise; abstract is a single unstructured paragraph followed by 1-6 key words from the official MNRAS list.
Layout: two columns (except the abstract), single line spaced; British English spellings ('centre', 'sulphur', 'acknowledgements'); 'km s^-1' not 'km/s'; SI plus astronomy-recognized units.

Initial submission: a single file (PDF, PS, Word, RTF or plain text) <=10 MB with figures included; supplementary material <=350 MB combined; LaTeX with the official mnras class (CTAN) is recommended; revisions highlight changes; accepted 'First Look' files as .zip/.tar.gz source archives.

Colour-blind-friendly figures requested 'where possible'; red and green in the same figure is particularly problematic; recommended tools: ColorBrewer and Color Oracle; coloured/shaded table cells are unsupported in the web version.
Long lists of citations should be avoided unless the articles cited are directly relevant.
Line weights must withstand significant reduction in size (minimum 0.3 pt at final size); no line-numbering requirement is stated.
